entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Heard Mohd. Ayub, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Vishwa Deepak Mishra, learned Aga for
the State and perused the material placed on record.

2. This first bail application has been filed with a prayer to release the applicant on bail in Case
Crime No.101 of 2024, registered under Sections 498A, 304-B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dp Act,
Police Station Ikdil, District Etawah, during pendency of the trial.

entities.text:
Dp Act,
Police Station Ikdil, District Etawah
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3.  As per prosecution story, marriage of applicant's son was solemnized with the deceased on 25.12.2023, thereafter, in-laws of the deceased physically and mentally tortured her for additional demand of dowry and when the demand of dowry was not fulfilled, the in-laws members murdered her by throttling.

Smt Shakuntala vs State Of U.P. on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48700828/

entities.text: Smt Shakuntala vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
The applicant has been intentionally dragged in the present case.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 03.04.2024.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, she will not misuse the liberty of bail and co-operate in trial.

5. Per contra, learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer of the applicant and submits that as per post mortem report, ante mortem injuries are (1) Contusion of eye approx 7x6 cm over left angle of muscle.
(2) Contusion of eye approx 2x1.5 cm sub mental eye 2 cm behind trip and claim on left side.
(3) Contusion of eye approx 2.5x1 cm on rt. side of neck, lateral to thyroid cartridge on right side.

He further submitted that deceased has died within four months of her marriage in her matrimonial house and applicant, being head of the family members, has to prove his innocence.
Deceased has subjected to cruelty and on account of throttling, she died, hence, the applicant is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.
6.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and looking to seriousness and gravity of offence, evidence, complicity of the accused,
I do not find it is a fit case for bail to the applicant.
7. Accordingly, the bail application of the applicant- Smt. Shakuntala, involved in the aforesaid case crime, is hereby rejected at this stage.

Order Date :- 30.9.2024 Nitin Verma  Smt Shakuntala vs State Of U.P. on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48700828/
